Leaders of Germany, Hungary, Sweden and Romania, along with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, congratulated Serbia's opposition Student List on its victory in the October 25 snap parliamentary elections, welcoming the high voter turnout and pledging support for democratic reforms and European integration. Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar spoke by phone with Student List leaders, congratulating them on their victory. "I am glad to hear how much strength you drew during this difficult battle from our electoral victory in April," Magyar wrote on Facebook. He also noted that Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic had conceded defeat after the student movement secured an absolute majority. "Celebrations have begun in the streets across Serbia. Does this look familiar?" he added. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz welcomed the result and reaffirmed Berlin's support for Serbia's EU aspirations. "Serbia's parliamentary elections have delivered a clear result. Congratulations to the Student List! With its demands for the rule of law, the fight against corruption and fundamental freedoms, it has won the people's support. We will actively support Serbia's European path," Merz wrote on X. Romanian President Nicusor Dan congratulated Serbian citizens on the historic vote, which recorded the highest turnout in decades. He expressed Romania's readiness to work with the new government to advance Serbia's European integration and strengthen bilateral relations. Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson also praised the Student List's decisive victory and record voter participation. "This is an opportunity to strengthen democracy, the rule of law and the fight against corruption," he wrote on X, pledging continued Swedish support for Serbia's EU-related reforms. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky described the election result as the beginning of a new chapter in Serbia's history. "We wish Serbia success, genuine development and warm relations with the European community," Zelensky said. He thanked Serbia for respecting Ukraine's independence and expressed his willingness to expand cooperation between the two countries. "We want all the good hopes of the Serbian people to come true," the Ukrainian president added. The Student List won 52.9% of the vote in the October 25 elections, defeating Aleksandar Vucic's United Serbia coalition, which received 38.8%. The "Ivica Dacic – Factor of Stability" list secured 2.2%, Authentic Right won 0.9%, and European Serbia received 0.3%.
